title: Model-Adaptive Tool Necessity Reveals the Knowing-Doing Gap in LLM Tool Use
abstract: arXiv:2605.14038v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as autonomous agents that must decide when to answer directly vs. when to invoke external tools. Prior work studying adaptive tool use has largely treated tool necessity as a model-agnostic property, annotated by human or LLM judge, and mostly cover cases where the answer is obvious (e.g., fetching the weather vs. paraphrasing text). However, tool necessity in the wild is more nuanced due to the divergence of capability boundaries across models: a problem solvable by a strong model on its own may still require tools for a weaker one. In this work, we introduce a model-adaptive definition of tool-necessity, grounded in each model's empirical performance. Following this definition, we compare the necessity against observed tool-call behavior across four models on arithmetic and factual QA dataset, and find substantial mismatches of 26.5-54.0% and 30.8-41.8%, respectively. translated_title: 模型自适应的工具必要性揭示了LLM工具使用中的“知行差距”
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）日益作为自主智能体运行，必须决定何时直接回答、何时调用外部工具。以往研究自适应工具使用的工作大多将工具必要性视为与模型无关的属性，由人类或LLM评判者进行标注，且主要涵盖答案显而易见的情况（例如获取天气 vs. 改写文本）。然而，现实中的工具必要性更为微妙，因为不同模型的能力边界存在差异：一个强模型能够独立解决的问题，对于较弱的模型来说可能仍然需要借助工具。在这项工作中，我们提出了一种基于各模型实际经验表现的模型自适应工具必要性定义。根据这一定义，我们在算术和事实问答数据集上，将工具必要性与四个模型实际观察到的工具调用行为进行对比，发现二者分别存在26.5%-54.0%和30.8%-41.8%的显著不匹配。为了诊断这一（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了基于各模型自身能力表现的“模型自适应工具必要性”新定义，并发现在算术和事实问答任务中，模型的实际工具调用行为与真实的工具必要性之间存在高达26.5%-54.0%的不匹配，揭示了LLM工具使用中的“知行差距”。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a model-adaptive definition of tool necessity grounded in each model's empirical performance, revealing substantial mismatches (26.5%-54.0% on arithmetic and 30.8%-41.8% on factual QA) between when tools are actually needed and when models call them—the "knowing-doing gap" in LLM tool use.
